audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Sett, Skill, Yone, Yone, Sett, Yone, Yone while the whys under rows 1-3 say Haymaker 'wins every trade' at 2 and that levels 3 and 4-5 are even.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Sett, Sett, Skill, Skill, Sett, Yone, Yone, which matches every whys[] string. Row 1 was labelled Skill against text describing a Sett win; rows 2 and 3 were labelled Yone against text describing an even lane. 48.55% over 3969 games also does not support Yone owning the mid-lane levels.
audit.corrected: Set rows 1, 2 and 3 to Sett, Skill, Skill in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every 'wait for the cooldown' instruction is unnumbered.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, The Show Stopper 120/100/80s. Those three numbers are the whole lane clock and none of them appear on the page.
audit.corrected: Put 18s on Haymaker and 16s on Facebreaker in the phases and Do's so 'trade on the cooldown' becomes countable.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Facebreaker as a straightforward grab-and-stun that sets up the ultimate, and never states its condition.
audit.why: Riot's E text: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' In a solo lane with no ally or second target opposite you, Facebreaker slows — it does not stun. That single fact decides whether his level-6 combo is a kill or a slow you can walk out of, and the page currently teaches the player to fear the wrong version of it. Second gap: The Show Stopper carries you through the air and slams you, so neither Mortal Steel's Q3 dash nor Fate Sealed is available while it resolves — the missingInteractions 'dash-denied' entry is real.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker only stuns when someone is on his far side; alone you are slowed instead. Once The Show Stopper picks you up, Q3 and Fate Sealed are both unavailable, so the escape has to happen before he casts.

audit.why: Haymaker's centre deals true damage, so stacking raw armour is the wrong answer — the page already leads with Blade of the Ruined King and Executioner's Calling rather than resistances, which is right.
sources: enemyKit W trueDamage flag and text

edits.before: W shield-grit covers every exchange you start. Only take the trade when Sett's Haymaker is down.
edits.after: Haymaker banks the damage you deal and returns it as true damage. Trade only on its 18-second cooldown.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Sett must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Even now: Facebreaker stuns only if someone is on his far side — alone in lane, you are slowed instead.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Haymaker's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Even lane: trade on Haymaker's 18-second cooldown and Facebreaker's 16 seconds, and give him nothing while either one is up.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Sett's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: The Show Stopper carries you through the air and slams you — no Q3, no Fate Sealed once it starts. Refuse the 6 all-in.

edits.before: Shield + true damage. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Shield plus true damage in the centre, 18s at rank 1. Bait it, then commit.

edits.before: Level 6 favors Sett because E into Show Stopper is a full-combo kill.
edits.after: Level 6 favors Sett: Facebreaker into The Show Stopper kills you.

edits.before: Around your first item the lane starts to even; keep dodging Facebreaker (E) grab, because his kit is still front-loaded and his W shield punishes greedy trades.
edits.after: Around your first item the lane evens; Facebreaker (E) only stuns if someone is on his far side, so alone you are slowed — walk out rather than panic-dashing into his W.

edits.before: At level 2 his Haymaker true-damage shield wins every trade.
edits.after: At level 2 his Haymaker true-damage shield wins the trades.
